$comment: Fin-City Park · Advanced (ages 13-18). Many questions use randomized vars and computed answers (answerExpr). ${x} formats as money.

questions.prompt: Which account is best for money you'll spend this week?
questions.explanation: Checking is built for frequent deposits and spending. CDs and retirement accounts lock money up.

questions.prompt: You deposit ${P} at {r}% simple interest per year. How much interest after {t} years?
questions.explanation: I = P × r × t = ${P} × {r}% × {t} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: ${P} grows at {r}% compounded monthly for {t} years. What is the final balance?
A savings account advertises {r}% APR compounded monthly. What is its APY?
questions.explanation: APY = (1 + APR/12)^12 − 1 = {ANSWER:pct}. APY is a bit higher than APR because interest compounds.

questions.prompt: Using the Rule of 72, about how many years does it take money to double at {r}% per year?
questions.explanation: 72 ÷ {r} ≈ {ANSWER} years.

questions.prompt: Your take-home pay is ${N}/month. Using the 50/30/20 rule, how much goes to savings and debt payoff?
questions.explanation: 20% of ${N} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Under 50/30/20, which belongs in the 50% 'needs' bucket?
choices: Extra principal payments on a loan
questions.explanation: Required payments (rent, utilities, groceries, minimum debt payments) are needs. Extra payments go in the 20% bucket.

questions.prompt: You skip a $60 concert to work a shift that pays $80. What is the opportunity cost of working?
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative you gave up, here, the concert experience.

questions.prompt: A savings account earns {n}% a year while inflation is {i}% a year. What is the real return per year (%)? Use (1 + rate) ÷ (1 + inflation) − 1.
questions.explanation: Real return = (1 + {n}%)/(1 + {i}%) − 1 ≈ {ANSWER:pct}. A negative real return means your buying power shrinks.

questions.prompt: Your card limit is ${L} and your balance is ${B}. What is your utilization (%)?
questions.explanation: Utilization = balance ÷ limit = ${B} ÷ ${L} = {ANSWER:pct}. Under 30% is healthy; under 10% is best.

questions.prompt: Which factor matters MOST for a FICO-style credit score?
questions.explanation: Payment history is about 35% of the score. Income isn't part of the score at all.

questions.prompt: You pay your credit card's full statement balance every month. How much interest do you pay?
choices: The APR on the full balance
questions.explanation: Paying the full statement balance by the due date keeps the grace period, no interest.

questions.prompt: A card has a balance of ${B} at {a}% APR. How much interest is charged for one month if nothing is paid?
questions.explanation: Monthly interest = balance × APR/12 = ${B} × {a}%/12 = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: A ${P} personal loan at {a}% APR for {n} months. What is the monthly payment?
questions.explanation: PMT = P·i / (1 − (1+i)^−n) with i = {a}%/12 → ${ANSWER} per month.

questions.prompt: Same loan: ${P} at {a}% for {n} months. How much TOTAL interest will you pay?
questions.explanation: Total paid = payment × {n} = ${P} + interest. Interest ≈ ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Your monthly expenses are ${E}. How big should a 3-month emergency fund be?
questions.explanation: 3 × ${E} = ${ANSWER}. Experts suggest 3–6 months of expenses.

questions.prompt: You deposit ${C} at the end of every month into an account earning {r}% APR (monthly compounding). How much after {y} years?
A 12-month CD pays 5.0% APY; savings pays 4.2% APY. Breaking the CD early costs 3 months' interest. When is the CD the better choice?
choices: You won’t need the money for 12 months
You might need the money next month
Always, a higher rate always wins
Never, savings is always more flexible
questions.explanation: CDs trade flexibility for a higher rate. If you might need the cash, the penalty can erase the advantage.

questions.prompt: Your checking balance is $120 and you swipe your debit card for $150. With overdraft coverage, what usually happens?
choices: It goes through and you pay an overdraft fee
The bank covers the difference for free
Your savings start earning more interest
It is declined: debit cards can’t overdraw
questions.explanation: Overdraft 'protection' often charges a fee (around $35). Many people opt out and let the card decline instead.

questions.prompt: Your checkbook shows ${A}. The bank statement shows ${S}, but a ${c} check you wrote hasn't cleared and you forgot to record a ${f} fee. Statement − uncleared check = ? (should equal checkbook − fee)
questions.explanation: ${S} − ${c} = ${ANSWER}, which equals your checkbook ${A} minus the ${f} fee. Reconciled!

questions.prompt: Which tax is a flat percentage of every paycheck regardless of income (up to a cap)?
questions.explanation: Social Security is 6.2% of wages up to an annual cap. Income tax is progressive.

questions.prompt: Fin City sales tax is 6%. You buy items totaling ${p}. What do you pay at checkout?
A home costs ${H}. A 20% down payment would be…
questions.explanation: 20% × ${H} = ${ANSWER}. A 20% down payment usually avoids mortgage insurance.

questions.prompt: A ${L} 30-year mortgage at {a}% APR. What is the monthly principal & interest payment?
questions.explanation: PMT with i = {a}%/12 and n = 360 → ${ANSWER} per month.

questions.prompt: On a ${L} 30-year mortgage at {a}%, how much total interest is paid over the full term?
questions.explanation: Payment × 360 − principal = ${ANSWER}. Interest can be more than the loan itself!

questions.prompt: Which usually makes renting the better choice than buying?
choices: You expect to move within 2 years
Home prices are rising fast and you have a big down payment
questions.explanation: Buying has big one-time costs (closing, selling fees). Short stays rarely recover them.

questions.prompt: A daily ${c} coffee habit costs how much per year (365 days)?
questions.explanation: ${c} × 365 = ${ANSWER} per year.

questions.prompt: If you instead invested that ${m} per month at 7% (monthly compounding) for 10 years, about how much would you have?
questions.explanation: FV of ${m}/month for 120 months at 7%/12 ≈ ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: A charity raised ${R}; it spent ${O} on overhead. What percent went to overhead?
questions.explanation: ${O} ÷ ${R} = {ANSWER:pct}. Lower overhead usually means more goes to the cause (though some overhead is normal).

questions.prompt: Net worth equals…
questions.explanation: Net worth = everything you own (assets) − everything you owe (liabilities). Income − expenses is cash flow.

questions.prompt: Assets: cash ${a}, savings ${s}, car worth ${c}. Debts: car loan ${l}, credit card ${d}. Net worth?
Which are red flags in a message claiming to be from your bank? (Select all)
choices: Urgent: 'Act within 10 minutes or your account closes'
Asks you to confirm your full PIN
Greets you by your nickname and shows the last 4 digits of your card
Says to call the number on the back of your card
questions.explanation: Urgency, look-alike domains and PIN requests are classic phishing signs. Calling the number on your card is the safe move.

questions.prompt: Your plan has a ${D} deductible and pays 80% after that. A ${B} medical bill arrives. How much do YOU pay?
questions.explanation: You pay the ${D} deductible + 20% of the remaining ${B} − ${D} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: You earn ${w}/hour and work {h} hours a week for 50 weeks. What is your annual gross pay?
What does 'diversification' reduce?
choices: The taxes you owe on gains
questions.explanation: Owning many companies reduces the damage any one can do. Market-wide risk remains.

questions.prompt: Two loans: ${P} at {a}% for 36 months vs. the same at {a}% for 60 months. Which is true?
choices: 60 months: lower payment, more total interest
They cost the same in total
The 36-month loan has the lower payment
questions.explanation: Longer terms lower the monthly payment but you pay interest for more months, raising total cost.

questions.prompt: Items total ${p} before Fin City’s 6% sales tax. The customer pays with a $100 bill. Change due?
questions.explanation: With tax the total is ${p} × 1.06, rounded to the cent. $100 minus that total = ${ANSWER}.
questions.hint: Add the 6% tax before working out the change.

questions.prompt: You have $4,000 of card debt at 24% APR and $4,000 in savings earning 4%. A smart move is usually…
choices: Pay off most of the card, keep a small cushion
Keep both as they are and pay the minimum
Move the savings into a 12-month CD
Open a second card to spread the balance
questions.explanation: Paying off 24% debt is like earning a guaranteed 24% return, far better than 4%. Keep a little cash for emergencies.

questions.prompt: Prices rise {i}% per year. What will a ${p} item cost in {t} years?
How many years for money to double at exactly {r}% compounded annually? (Use ln: t = ln 2 / ln(1+r))
questions.explanation: t = ln 2 / ln(1 + {r}%) = {ANSWER} years. Compare with the Rule of 72 estimate: 72/{r}.
